Cluster and GraphSAINT subgraph loaders

Source: R/subgraph-loaders.R
cluster_loader.Rd

Loaders that train node models on whole subgraphs instead of sampled neighborhoods. Pass one to train_graph_model() as loader; every batch is an induced subgraph, the loss uses the training nodes inside it, and validation uses the full graph.

Usage

cluster_loader(
  g,
  num_parts = 10L,
  clusters_per_batch = 1L,
  method = c("louvain", "random"),
  shuffle = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

saint_loader(
  g,
  batch_size = 100L,
  walk_length = 2L,
  num_steps = 10L,
  sample_coverage = 20L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

g

A graph_data object.

num_parts

Number of parts.

clusters_per_batch

Parts combined into one batch.

method

"louvain" or "random".

shuffle

Shuffle parts every epoch.

seed

Optional seed; the caller's random stream is left untouched.

batch_size

Number of random walk roots per batch.

walk_length

Steps per walk.

num_steps

Batches per epoch.

sample_coverage

Number of subgraphs pre-sampled per node (on average) to estimate normalization; 0 disables normalization.

Value

A loader of class subgraph_loader; loader_batches() returns a list of graph_data batches whose node_ids hold original node indices.

Details

  • cluster_loader() follows Cluster-GCN (Chiang et al. 2019): the graph is partitioned once into num_parts parts and each batch is the subgraph induced by clusters_per_batch randomly chosen parts, including the edges between them. With method = "louvain", nodes are ordered by Louvain community (igraph's cluster_louvain() on the undirected view) and then by breadth first search order, and the ordering is cut into num_parts parts of equal size, so parts follow communities where sizes allow; method = "random" assigns nodes at random. METIS is not used.

  • saint_loader() follows the GraphSAINT random walk sampler (Zeng et al. 2020): each batch is the subgraph induced by the nodes visited by batch_size random walks of length walk_length from uniformly drawn roots. Normalization coefficients are estimated from sample_coverage pre-sampled subgraphs, as in PyTorch Geometric's GraphSAINTSampler: each batch carries node_norm (loss weight \(\propto 1 / p_v\)) and edge weights multiplied by \(p_v / p_{uv}\) (aggregator normalization), where \(p\) are empirical inclusion frequencies. The trainer weights the per node loss by node_norm for the built in losses and for loss functions with a reduction argument.

Batches are drawn in R on the CPU.

References

Chiang et al. (2019) Cluster-GCN. Zeng et al. (2020) GraphSAINT: graph sampling based inductive learning method.

Examples

g <- split_nodes(dataset_sbm(c(40, 40, 40), seed = 1), seed = 1)
cl <- cluster_loader(g, num_parts = 6, clusters_per_batch = 2, seed = 1)
lengths(cl$parts)
#> [1] 20 20 20 20 20 20
vapply(loader_batches(cl), num_nodes, 1L)
#> [1] 40 40 40
sl <- saint_loader(g, batch_size = 10, walk_length = 3, seed = 1)
summary(loader_batches(sl)[[1]]$node_norm)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#> 0.01625 0.02708 0.03095 0.03255 0.03824 0.06500
